name: Caesar against Pompey
intro: From the Rubicon to Pharsalus, January 49 to August 48 BC. The Senate has ordered you, Gaius Julius Caesar, conqueror of Gaul, to give up your army. Pompey the Great, once your ally and son-in-law, commands the Senate’s forces. This is the civil war that ends the Roman Republic.
debrief: Caesar crossed the Rubicon in January 49 BC and swept through Italy. At Corfinium he pardoned his enemies. Pompey escaped from Brundisium to Greece. Caesar first beat Pompey’s legions in Spain at Ilerda, then crossed the Adriatic in winter. At Dyrrachium he tried to wall in Pompey’s larger army, but Pompey broke through and Caesar suffered his worst defeat. Retreating into Thessaly, he stormed Gomphi to feed his men. At Pharsalus, a hidden fourth line of cohorts routed Pompey’s cavalry and the Pompeian army broke. Pompey fled to Egypt and was murdered. The other choices are what-ifs.

win: The fourth line routs the cavalry.
lose: Labienus’s horse rides round the legions.
Pompey returns to Rome in triumph.

decisions.title: The Rubicon
decisions.text: January 49 BC. The Senate has ordered you to give up your army or be declared an enemy of the state. Pompey commands the Senate’s forces. You stand at the Rubicon, the border of Italy, with a single legion, the Thirteenth.

hint.text: Pompey’s legions are scattered across Italy and Spain and not yet ready.

scout.text: Speed is everything: Pompey is not ready.

choices.label: Cross the river tonight

fx.text: ‘The die is cast.’ You cross with the Thirteenth and race south. Town after town opens its gates.

choices.label: Wait in Gaul for all your legions to arrive

fx.text: Pompey uses the weeks to raise new levies.

choices.label: Offer the Senate one last compromise and wait

fx.text: The Senate refuses and calls up more troops.

decisions.title: Corfinium
decisions.text: Lucius Domitius Ahenobarbus, your bitter enemy, holds the hill town of Corfinium with thirty cohorts, against Pompey’s advice.

choices.label: Surround it, then pardon them all

fx.text: Trapped before help can come, Domitius’s soldiers hand him over. You let him and his officers go free and take his cohorts into your army. Italy hears of your mercy.
Corfinium surrenders after a siege. You pardon them all.

choices.label: Storm it before Pompey can send help

fx.text: The walls are strong and your men die on them.

choices.label: Bypass it and chase Pompey to the coast

fx.text: Domitius’s thirty cohorts stay behind you.

decisions.title: Brundisium
decisions.text: Pompey has fallen back to the port of Brundisium to take his army across the sea to Greece, where his allies and ships wait.

hint.text: Half his army has already sailed. The ships will come back for the rest.

choices.label: Build moles to block the harbour mouth

fx.text: Your men push rafts and earth into the harbour mouth, but Pompey slips out by night with the rest of his army.

choices.label: Storm the walls before the ships return

fx.text: The walls hold and the ships return.

choices.label: Let him go and secure Italy and Rome

fx.text: You let Pompey go and take Rome, its treasury and its grain.

decisions.title: A leader without an army
decisions.text: Italy is yours, but Pompey’s best legions are in Spain under his generals, and you have no fleet to follow him to Greece.

hint.text: You have a saying: first the army without a leader, then the leader without an army.

choices.label: March on Spain first

fx.text: You march to Spain and, at Ilerda, outmanoeuvre Pompey’s generals until their armies surrender without a battle.

choices.label: Build a fleet and chase Pompey to Greece now

fx.text: Spain’s legions march on Italy behind you.

choices.label: Hold Italy and wait for Pompey to come back

fx.text: Pompey grows stronger in the East every month.

decisions.title: The winter sea
decisions.text: January 48 BC. Pompey’s admiral Bibulus patrols the Adriatic with a great fleet. You have only enough ships for half your army. No one sails in winter.

hint.text: Bibulus does not expect anyone to cross in winter.

choices.label: Cross in winter with half the army

fx.text: With Spain safe behind you, you cross with seven legions and land on the coast of Epirus before Bibulus can react. Antony brings the rest months later.
You land in Epirus, but with enemies still behind you in the West.

choices.label: Wait for spring and more ships

fx.text: Pompey trains his army all winter.

choices.label: Send Antony first with the other half

fx.text: Bibulus catches part of the fleet.

decisions.title: Dyrrachium
decisions.text: Pompey is camped on the coast near Dyrrachium with a larger army, supplied by sea. Your men are short of food, eating bread made from roots.

hint.text: His army is bigger, but his horses are starving for grass.

choices.label: Wall in his whole army with siege lines

fx.text: Your men dig seventeen miles of lines around Pompey’s camp. His horses starve, but so do your men.

choices.label: Attack his camp at once

fx.text: His camp is too strong.

choices.label: March inland and make him follow you

fx.text: Pompey must leave the sea and his supplies to follow you.

decisions.title: The breakthrough
decisions.text: Deserters show Pompey a weak point at the southern end of your lines. At dawn his legions break through by land and sea.

hint.text: Your men are scattered along miles of lines.

scout.text: Pull back before you lose the army.

choices.label: Counter-attack with thirty-three cohorts

fx.text: Your counter-attack gets lost in the old camps and ditches. Your men panic and flee. You lose a thousand men and thirty-two standards. Pompey does not follow up. ‘Today the victory would have been theirs, if they had a leader who knew how to win,’ you say.
Your counter-attack is beaten back.

choices.label: Fall back in good order

fx.text: You pull your men back before Pompey can cut them off.

choices.label: Hold every point on the lines

fx.text: Your thin lines are pushed back.

decisions.title: Into Thessaly
decisions.text: You retreat east into Thessaly, short of food. Pompey follows, but the senators in his camp argue over who will hold which office after the war.

hint.text: The town of Gomphi has shut its gates on you.

scout.text: Your men need food and heart.

choices.label: Storm Gomphi

fx.text: You storm Gomphi in an afternoon. Your hungry men eat and drink their fill. Other towns open their gates.

choices.label: Go round it and march on toward Pompey

fx.text: Your men stay hungry.

choices.label: Ask Pompey for peace talks while you can

fx.text: Pompey’s senators laugh.

decisions.title: Pharsalus: the cavalry
decisions.text: August 48 BC, the plain of Pharsalus. Pompey has 47,000 men to your 22,000, and 7,000 horse to your 1,000. Labienus will lead the cavalry round your right.

hint.text: Pompey’s horsemen are young nobles who fear wounds to the face.

scout.text: Hide a fourth line of cohorts behind your right.

choices.label: Hide a fourth line behind the right

fx.text: You take six cohorts from your third line and hide them behind the Tenth. They wait with their javelins.

choices.label: Mass your cavalry on the right

fx.text: Your 1,000 horse cannot stop 7,000.

choices.label: Anchor your right on rough ground

fx.text: There is little rough ground on this plain.

decisions.title: Pharsalus: the charge
decisions.text: Labienus’s horse sweeps round your right. Pompey’s infantry waits, ordered not to advance.

hint.text: Strike the cavalry at their faces.

choices.label: Unleash the fourth line at their faces

fx.text: Your hidden cohorts charge the horsemen, thrusting their javelins at their faces. The cavalry panics and flees. Your third line goes in, and Pompey’s army breaks. Pompey rides to his camp, then flees to Egypt, where he is murdered.
The cavalry is driven off at great cost.

choices.label: Pull the right back to face the cavalry

fx.text: The cavalry is held, but Pompey’s legions advance.

choices.label: Charge Pompey’s infantry before the cavalry strikes

fx.text: Labienus’s horse falls on your rear.

italy.label: Weeks later
italy.title: Corfinium, in the hills of Italy

dyrr.label: Spring 48 BC
dyrr.title: Dyrrachium, on the coast of Illyria
